claims: As of April 2026, Pam Bondi was the former U.S. Attorney General.
As of April 2026, Pam Bondi faced calls for impeachment introduced by Representatives Summer Lee and Shri Thanedar.
President Trump fired Pam Bondi on April 2, 2026.
Rep. Summer Lee introduced H.Res.1119 in March 2026.
H.Res.1119 cited "high crimes and misdemeanors".
Rep. Shri Thanedar moved to introduce articles of impeachment against Pam Bondi.
The impeachment efforts focused on allegations of covering up the Epstein files.
The impeachment efforts focused on allegations of violating the Epstein Files Transparency Act.
The impeachment efforts focused on allegations of weaponizing the DOJ against political opponents.
Supporters of impeachment accused Pam Bondi of willfully withholding millions of documents related to the Jeffrey Epstein investigation past legal deadlines.
Supporters of impeachment accused Pam Bondi of protecting associates of Donald Trump.
Supporters of impeachment accused Pam Bondi of utilizing the DOJ to investigate political rivals.
The House Oversight Committee voted in a bipartisan manner to subpoena Pam Bondi regarding the handling of the Epstein files.
According to PBS News, Pam Bondi's tenure was marked by accusations of undermining the DOJ's independence.
According to PBS News, Pam Bondi's tenure was marked by major staff turnovers.
According to PBS News, Pam Bondi's tenure was marked by targeting critics of the administration.
Pam Bondi argued that the failure to release the Epstein files was due to the immense volume of the files.
Pam Bondi argued that the failure to release the Epstein files was due to necessary redactions for the files.
Rep. Dave Min continued to push for accountability after Pam Bondi's removal.
According to a statement on min.house.gov, Pam Bondi's firing did not absolve her of the alleged misconduct.
